new_with_buttons.md:
Creates a new `GtkInfoBar` with buttons.

Button text/response ID pairs should be listed, with a `NULL` pointer
ending the list. A response ID can be any positive number,
or one of the values in the `GtkResponseType` enumeration. If the
user clicks one of these dialog buttons, GtkInfoBar will emit
the [`InfoBar::response`](xref:gtk:Gtk.InfoBar#event:response) signal with the corresponding
response ID.

doc.brief: `GtkInfoBar` can be used to show messages to the user without a dialog.
doc.deprecated_md:
There is no replacement in GTK for an "info bar" widget;
  you can use [`Revealer`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Revealer) with a [`Box`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Box) containing a
  [`Label`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Label) and an optional [`Button`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Button), according to
  your application's design.

add_action_widget.brief: Add an activatable widget to the action area of a `GtkInfoBar`.
add_action_widget.md:
Add an activatable widget to the action area of a `GtkInfoBar`.

This also connects a signal handler that will emit the
[`InfoBar::response`](xref:gtk:Gtk.InfoBar#event:response) signal on the message area
when the widget is activated. The widget is appended to the
end of the message areas action area.

add_button.brief: Adds a button with the given text.
add_button.md:
Adds a button with the given text.

Clicking the button will emit the [`InfoBar::response`](xref:gtk:Gtk.InfoBar#event:response)
signal with the given response_id. The button is appended to the
end of the info bar's action area. The button widget is returned,
but usually you don't need it.

add_buttons.md:
Adds multiple buttons.

This is the same as calling [`InfoBar.add_button()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.InfoBar#method:add_button)
repeatedly. The variable argument list should be `NULL`-terminated
as with [`InfoBar.new_with_buttons()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.InfoBar#constructor:new_with_buttons). Each button must have both
text and response ID.

add_child.brief: Adds a widget to the content area of the info bar.
add_child.md: Adds a widget to the content area of the info bar.

get_message_type.brief: Returns the message type of the message area.
get_message_type.md: Returns the message type of the message area.

get_revealed.brief: Returns whether the info bar is currently revealed.
get_revealed.md: Returns whether the info bar is currently revealed.

get_show_close_button.brief: Returns whether the widget will display a standard close button.
get_show_close_button.md: Returns whether the widget will display a standard close button.

remove_action_widget.brief: Removes a widget from the action area of `info_bar`.
remove_action_widget.md:
Removes a widget from the action area of `info_bar`.

The widget must have been put there by a call to
[`InfoBar.add_action_widget()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.InfoBar#method:add_action_widget) or [`InfoBar.add_button()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.InfoBar#method:add_button).

remove_child.brief: Removes a widget from the content area of the info bar.
remove_child.md: Removes a widget from the content area of the info bar.

response.brief: Emits the “response” signal with the given `response_id`.
response.md: Emits the “response” signal with the given `response_id`.

set_default_response.brief: Sets the last widget in the info bar’s action area with the given response_id as the default widget for the dialog.
set_default_response.md:
Sets the last widget in the info bar’s action area with
the given response_id as the default widget for the dialog.

Pressing “Enter” normally activates the default widget.

Note that this function currently requires `info_bar` to
be added to a widget hierarchy.

set_message_type.brief: Sets the message type of the message area.
set_message_type.md:
Sets the message type of the message area.

GTK uses this type to determine how the message is displayed.

set_response_sensitive.brief: Sets the sensitivity of action widgets for `response_id`.
set_response_sensitive.md:
Sets the sensitivity of action widgets for `response_id`.

Calls `gtk_widget_set_sensitive (widget, setting)` for each
widget in the info bars’s action area with the given `response_id`.
A convenient way to sensitize/desensitize buttons.

set_revealed.md:
Sets whether the `GtkInfoBar` is revealed.

Changing this will make `info_bar` reveal or conceal
itself via a sliding transition.

Note: this does not show or hide `info_bar` in the
[`Widget:visible`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:visible) sense, so revealing has no effect
if [`Widget:visible`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:visible) is `FALSE`.

set_show_close_button.brief: If true, a standard close button is shown.
set_show_close_button.md:
If true, a standard close button is shown.

When clicked it emits the response %GTK_RESPONSE_CLOSE.

message-type.md:
The type of the message.

The type may be used to determine the appearance of the info bar.

revealed.brief: Whether the info bar shows its contents.
revealed.md: Whether the info bar shows its contents.

show-close-button.brief: Whether to include a standard close button.
show-close-button.md: Whether to include a standard close button.

close.brief: Gets emitted when the user uses a keybinding to dismiss the info bar.
close.md:
Gets emitted when the user uses a keybinding to dismiss the info bar.

The ::close signal is a [keybinding signal](class.SignalAction.html).

The default binding for this signal is the Escape key.

response.brief: Emitted when an action widget is clicked.
response.md:
Emitted when an action widget is clicked.

The signal is also emitted when the application programmer
calls [`InfoBar.response()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.InfoBar#method:response). The `response_id` depends
on which action widget was clicked.
